channel.title: The PHP Dictionary — Recent Changes
channel.description: Recently added or updated entries in the PHP Dictionary.

item.title: Folklore
item.description: The PHP community's folklore is all the non-language related creations, that serves as a link in the community.

item.title: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
item.description: CISA, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, is the US federal agency that works on the security and resilience of critical infrastructure.

item.title: ABI
item.description: An ABI, or Application Binary Interface, is the contract at the compiled level:

item.title: Throwable
item.description: ``Throwable`` is a PHP native interface, which is required for any object to be used with thrown, such as ``Exception`` and ``Error``.

item.title: array_filter()
item.description: ``array_filter()`` is a native PHP function that filters elements of an array using a callback.

item.title: Database
item.description: A database is an organized set of data, which may be queried.

item.title: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL)
item.description: ETL, for Extract, Transform, Load, is a three-stage process used to move data from one or more source systems into a target system.

item.title: Extensions
item.description: Extensions are a custom way to add features to software.

item.title: Monitoring
item.description: Monitoring is the process of observing, tracking, and analyzing the performance, health, and behavior of applications or infrastructure over time.

item.title: Security
item.description: Security involves implementing measures and best practices to protect the application and its data from malicious attacks and vulnerabilities.

item.title: Thread
item.description: A thread is a set of instructions, designed to be executed independently from the parent process.

item.title: Types Erasure
item.description: Type Erasure is the removal of type annotations from the source code when going to production.

item.title: Type Parametricity
item.description: Type parametricity, or parametric polymorphism, is the ability to write a function, class, or interface once and have it work uniformly over any type, with that type supplied as a parameter rather than hard-coded.

item.title: Vulnerability
item.description: A vulnerability is a weakness or flaw in a computer system, software, hardware, or even a process that can be exploited by an attacker to perform unauthorized actions.

item.title: Erased Types
item.description: Erased types are type parameters or annotations that exist while the code is analysed or compiled, and are gone when the program runs.

item.title: Indexed Array
item.description: An indexed array is an array whose keys are only integers.

item.title: Index
item.description: An index, plural indices, may be several things:

item.title: Array Compaction
item.description: Array compaction is removing the gaps from an array's keys, so that the remaining elements are numbered again from 0 without holes.

item.title: Checked by Existence
item.description: Checked by existence describes a test that only asks whether something is present, without looking at its value.

item.title: Try-catch
item.description: Try-catch is a PHP command, which runs a block of code, and catches some configured exceptions that the block may throw.

item.title: throw
item.description: Throw is the keyword which raises an exception.

item.title: Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)
item.description: SSL, the Secure Sockets Layer, is a cryptographic protocol designed to provide communications security over a computer network and on the Web.

item.title: Asymmetric Cryptography
item.description: Asymmetric cryptography, also called public-key cryptography, is a method of encrypting and authenticating data using two mathematically linked keys, a public key and a private key.

item.title: Resource Leak
item.description: A resource leak occurs when a resource, such as a file handle, database connection, network socket, or stream, is opened but never properly closed.

item.title: Math
item.description: PHP offers many math features.

item.title: Ignored Catch
item.description: ``catch`` does not check that the caught exception exists.

item.title: Finally
item.description: Finally is the default clause of a try-catch expression.

item.title: Exception
item.description: Exceptions are a mechanism for handling errors and exceptional situations in a more structured and controlled way compared to traditional error handling methods like using error codes or ``die()`` statements.

item.title: Exception Handler
item.description: The exception handler is a default or custom function, which is called once an exception has exhausted all available ``try-catch`` blocks.

item.title: Catch
item.description: ``catch`` is the complement clause of try.

item.title: Canary Test
item.description: A canary test is a deliberately trivial test that is expected to pass.

item.title: Bloom Filter
item.description: A Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic data structure used to test whether an element is a member of a set.

item.title: Anonymous Catch
item.description: Traditionally, the catch statement requires specifying both an Exception class and an identifier variable to hold the caught exception.

item.title: __halt_compiler()
item.description: ``__halt_compiler()`` halts the execution of the compiler.

item.title: Abstract Keyword
item.description: PHP has ``abstract`` classes, properties and methods.

item.title: And Operator
item.description: ``and`` is the logical operator of the same name.

item.title: Ahead Of Time
item.description: Ahead-of-time compilation, ``AOT``, is the process of compiling source code to machine code before execution, as opposed to at runtime.

item.title: Application Programming Interface (API)
item.description: An API is a set of functions and procedures allowing the creation of applications that access the features or data of another service.

item.title: Argon2
item.description: Argon2 is a modern, secure, and highly efficient password hashing algorithm.

item.title: Array, []
item.description: ``array`` is the array structure.

item.title: array_change_key_case()
item.description: ``array_change_key_case()`` is a native PHP function that returns a copy of an array where all the string keys are converted to lowercase or uppercase.

item.title: Arrow Functions
item.description: Arrow functions, introduced with the ``fn`` keyword, are a type of closure with a specific syntax.

item.title: Artifact
item.description: An artifact refers to any intermediate or final output that is produced during the development process.

item.title: As
item.description: The as operator has several usages:

item.title: Authorization Header
item.description: The Authorization header carries the credentials that a client sends to a server to authenticate a request.

item.title: Base Conversion
item.description: Base conversion turns an integer written in one numeric base into the same value written in another base.

item.title: Bearer Token
item.description: A bearer token is an access credential sent with an HTTP request to prove the caller's identity.

item.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
item.description: Object Level Authorization is a mechanism that checks if a user has the right to access or execute an action on a specific object.

item.title: Break
item.description: ``break`` is a control structure, which ends execution of the current ``for``, ``foreach``, ``while``, ``do-while`` or ``switch`` structure.

item.title: Callables
item.description: A callable is an object that can pass the ``callable`` type.
